Visualizer for Amazon Music

Does Amazon Music have a visualizer on Mac?

By Syd Lawrence, a visual artist and developer who makes Vibresia. Facts last checked 2 November 2026; updated 2 November 2026.

Not that we could find: the visual Amazon documents for its web app is lyrics that scroll with the song, not a visualiser. On a Mac, Amazon Music plays in the browser at music.amazon.com. To get visuals that follow it, use an app that listens to the Mac's sound: Vibresia, which we make, does that for free.

Amazon Music on a Mac today

The dependable way to play Amazon Music on a Mac is the web player, which works in Safari, Chrome, Firefox and Edge. Whether Amazon still offers a separate Mac app is unclear: a post from Amazon in February 2025, relayed on Apple's forums, says it was discontinued. A visualiser that hears the Mac's system audio doesn't mind which one you use.

In the full-screen player, Amazon shows lyrics that scroll in time with the song. Like Deezer's, they follow the words rather than the sound, so they sit happily beside a visualiser on another display.

How to get visuals for Amazon Music on a Mac

Vibresia is a free Mac app that listens to the Mac's system audio, so it doesn't need Amazon Music to support it. Install it, allow it to hear system audio the first time it asks, and play something in Amazon Music. The visuals follow the music straight away: it picks out the beat, the bass, mids and treble and the tempo on the Mac, and nothing is uploaded.

It has 18 built-in scenes, and Auto Scan moves between them on the beat. If you want something of your own, a scene is a single GLSL function, or you can describe one to an AI assistant and have it written for you. It needs macOS 14.2 or later, Apple silicon.

Why system audio is the way to do it

A visualiser built into one music app only sees that app. Apple's own visualiser is a good example: it only works with songs playing in the Music app. Listening to the Mac's system audio instead means one visualiser works with Amazon Music, with every other music app, with a browser tab and with a film, and keeps going when you switch between them.

Questions people ask

Does Amazon Music have a visualizer?

Not one that Amazon's help pages mention. The web app shows lyrics that scroll with the song. A Mac app that hears system audio, such as Vibresia, gives you visuals that follow Amazon Music.

It's unclear whether Amazon still offers one; a February 2025 post from Amazon says it was discontinued. The web player at music.amazon.com works in Safari, Chrome, Firefox and Edge.
